To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we performed a comprehensive methylome and transcriptome analysis of 10 breast cancers cell lines, 2) we identified 77 candidate genes overexpressed in breast cancer cell lines of basal like phenotype and 3) we identified 9 genes overexpressed both in basal-like breast cells and BRCA mutated cells.
we identified new therapeutic targets for basal-like breast cancers, which are among the most lethal tumors.

we performed Methyl-seq and RNA-seq of ten breast cancer cell lines and identified 77 genes that are overexpressed in the basal like breast cancer cell lines, and 9 genes overexpressed in breast cancer cells with BRCA1 mutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes that are overexpressed in the basal-like subtype and in BRCA1 mutated tumors and that could be used as therapeutic targets in breast cancer.
the development of new therapeutic approaches for triple-negative breast cancers and BRCA1 mutations.
the discovery of new therapeutic targets in basal-like breast tumors, and the development of new therapeutic strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
basal like breast cancer cells and/or BRCA1 mutated tumors could be targeted using antioxydative drugs and drugs targeting epithelial to meschymal transition and cell migration.
the BRCA1 gene is not the only gene involved in basal-like breast tumor development and that the basal-like phenotype is not only linked to BRCA mutation.
basal-like breast cancer is not a single entity but rather a group of tumors with different genetic and epigenetic profiles and different clinical outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a list of genes overexpressed in breast basal-like cancer cell lines and that these genes could be considered as potential therapeutic targets in basal-like breast tumor cells.
basal like breast cancer cells and cells with BRCA1 mutations have similar gene expression profiles and that these cells are highly migratory.
the overexpression of genes involved in antioxdation and cell migration is a common feature of basal like and BRCA1 breast cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BRCA1 mutated phenotype is not a basal-like breast cancer phenotype, but rather a basal-like breast tumor phenotype that is associated with a basal-like cell migration phenotype.
RNA-seq data can be used to find new therapeutic targets in breast cancer.
RNA-Seq analysis can help to find new potential therapeutic targets in breast cancers, even when Methyl-Seq analysis fails to confirm known tumor hypermethylating phenotype of basal-like cancers.
